name: Tosun Terzioğlu Garden
subtitle: Beside the Information Center · Outdoors
title: One person, one university, one garden

texts.short:
The person behind the name.
The garden is named after Tosun Terzioğlu, a mathematician and the founding rector of Sabancı University. Born in Istanbul in 1942, he built a career in research, teaching and science administration before helping establish this university.

What kind of university did he imagine?.
Tosun Hoca valued students who were curious and able to make their own decisions. His willingness to listen and his commitment to freedom of thought helped shape Sabancı’s university culture.

Knowing a campus through its trees.
Tosun Hoca took a close interest in the campus’s plants. He followed landscaping work and introduced trees and plants on campus tours. Remembering him through a garden connects with this part of his life.

Why a garden?.
After Tosun Terzioğlu died in 2016, this garden was created beside the Information Center in his memory. It opened on 30 June 2017. Its plants, water and places to rest recall his connection with nature. Pausing here can be a small way to spend time with his story.
texts.medium:
The person behind the name.
The story of this garden begins with the person it remembers. Tosun Terzioğlu was born in Istanbul in 1942. He studied mathematics in Newcastle and completed his doctorate in Frankfurt. Back in Turkey, he worked at Middle East Technical University and later served as president of TÜBİTAK, the national scientific research council.

In 1997, he became the founding rector of Sabancı University. The name on the garden therefore recalls both a scientist and an educator who helped shape the university around you.

What kind of university did he imagine?.
When a university is founded, its approach to learning develops alongside its buildings. Tosun Terzioğlu served as Sabancı’s founding rector from 1997 to 2009.

Colleagues remembered someone who listened carefully and disliked rigid hierarchies. In her memorial address, Ayşe Kadıoğlu connected these qualities with the university’s culture. The aim was to let students ask questions and develop their thinking freely. This chapter follows the influence that the person remembered by the garden had on the campus’s intellectual life.

Knowing a campus through its trees.
To get to know Tosun Hoca, let us move from the rector’s office to the campus paths. Nesrin Balkan’s memorial article describes his involvement in the landscaping that began in 1999. He took an interest in which plants were placed where and introduced them to students and staff on campus tours.

A 2017 memorial address also mentions wintersweet among the plants he was said to love. This detail helps explain why a garden is a meaningful memorial: its greenery recalls an interest that was already part of his life.

Why a garden?.
Tosun Terzioğlu died on 23 February 2016. Created to remember him on campus, the garden occupies approximately 2,500 square metres beside the Information Center. It opened on 30 June 2017.

The project description emphasized plants and trees he loved, flowing water, natural materials and places to sit and think. These choices brought his interest in nature together with the value he placed on listening and conversation.

We can therefore look for the story beyond the name on a sign. Resting here, being curious about the surroundings or talking with a friend can also be ways to connect with that memory.
texts.detailed:
The person behind the name.
When you enter a garden, you may first notice the trees, the water or somewhere to sit. Here, there is also a name: Tosun Terzioğlu. The journey behind that name began in Istanbul on 13 March 1942.

After Robert College, he studied mathematics at Newcastle, graduating in 1965. He completed his doctorate in Frankfurt in 1968, returned to Turkey and joined the mathematics department at Middle East Technical University. His academic career combined teaching, research and university administration. From 1992 to 1997, he served as president of TÜBİTAK, Turkey’s scientific research council.

His return to Istanbul in 1997 brought a new responsibility: becoming rector of Sabancı University while it was still being established. Experience gained in mathematics and science administration became part of building a new university. That is the first connection in this garden’s story: the person whose name you see was also part of this campus’s beginnings.

What kind of university did he imagine?.
Now look beyond the garden towards the campus buildings. If we understand a university’s founding only through its completed structures, we miss part of the story. Another question matters: what kind of environment will bring students and teachers together?

During his founding rectorship from 1997 to 2009, Tosun Terzioğlu helped shape that environment. At the 2017 memorial ceremony, Ayşe Kadıoğlu linked his modesty, willingness to listen and distance from rigid hierarchy with the university’s culture. She also emphasized his support for academic freedom.

At the same ceremony, his daughter Ayşecan Terzioğlu recalled an idea that excited him during the university’s founding: creating a place where knowledge could be produced and shared without the barriers of hierarchy. Her recollection connects his personality with his approach to university life. Later, when we consider the garden as a place to pause and talk, this idea will meet another part of the story.

Knowing a campus through its trees.
The previous chapter explored sharing knowledge. Tosun Hoca’s interest in campus plants offers an example beyond the classroom. Nesrin Balkan’s memorial article describes how closely he followed the landscaping that began after campus construction in 1999. He was interested in the choice of trees and plants, and where they would grow.

The article also recalls tours he organized for new students and interested staff, introducing the campus’s vegetation and natural features. The picture that emerges is of someone who knew the living things around him and enjoyed sharing that knowledge.

In her 2017 address, Ayşe Kadıoğlu mentioned wintersweet as one of the plants he was said to love. The presence of a favourite plant in a memorial speech suggests that his connection with nature also stayed in his colleagues’ memories. Now look at a plant nearby: wondering about its name, when it flowers or why it grows here is this chapter’s small invitation.

Why a garden?.
Let us return to where the story began: the garden. After Tosun Terzioğlu died on 23 February 2016, the university developed several ways to preserve his memory. This garden was one of them. It opened on 30 June 2017 on approximately 2,500 square metres beside the Information Center. Kartepe Peyzaj carried out the landscaping.

Before the garden was completed, its project description included plants and trees he loved, flowing water, natural materials and seating where people could rest and think. Ayşe Kadıoğlu described it as somewhere the university community could reflect and talk with one another.

Placed together, these details give meaning to the question “why a garden?” We can think of it as a place of remembrance where an interest in nature, curiosity and conversation can coexist.

At the end of this visit, you do not need to do anything grand. Notice a plant, look at the water or spend a few minutes talking. You first encountered a name; now you can read it alongside the story of a scientist, an educator and a person who cared about the natural world.

name: Information Center · IC
subtitle: Outside the building · Story coming soon
title: A journey that starts with a question

texts.short: The Information Center supports learning and research at Sabancı University. Its distinctive dome marks a place for finding information. Standing outside, think of something you would like to learn today.
texts.medium:
You are outside Sabancı University’s Information Center. Its large dome draws on Ottoman architecture. Behind it is a service that connects students, researchers, staff and alumni with information and documents.

For this proposed stop, look at the dome and consider a question that interests you. A research journey can begin with a small question rather than the title of a book.
texts.detailed:
The open space in front of the Information Center is the proposed research stop on our campus route. The university describes the building as a large domed structure inspired by Ottoman architecture. Its role is to support education and research.

The center helps users find the information they need. It serves students, academics, staff and alumni, and also welcomes external users under its access rules.

The story proposed for this stop follows the beginning of an investigation: choose a question, find relevant sources and compare what they tell you. As you learn, your first question may change. Look at the dome and consider a question you would like to explore. This visitor activity is an original narrative suggestion based on the center’s role.

name: Lake · Sports Center
subtitle: Outdoor lakeside stop · Story coming soon
title: The active shore of campus

texts.short: The proposed stop is outside the Sports Center, facing the lake. A running track surrounds the university’s artificial lake. Pause here and consider how movement fits into a day of learning.
texts.medium:
The proposed lakeside stop is outside the Sports Center. The university places it beside the Performing Arts Center, on the shore of the lake. A running track goes around the artificial lake.

This story would explore movement and rest between classes. Walking to think, taking a break with friends and exercising can all be parts of the same day. Look around the water and reflect on the time you make for yourself.
texts.detailed:
For the third stop, we propose the outdoor area beside the Sports Center, facing the lake. The university’s sports page locates the center next to the Performing Arts Center and on the lakeshore. It provides a concrete starting point for a story that can be experienced without entering a building. The exact stopping point and walking access still need to be checked on site.

The campus facilities page describes the lake as artificial and notes the running track around it. These details suggest a story about everyday campus life.

A university day includes more than lessons: movement, rest and time with friends also shape the experience. Looking around the lake, recall a short walk, an unexpected conversation or a pause to think. This is an original visitor activity based on the documented location, not a historical account of the lake’s construction.
